stats.note_on_absence: Torah #127 (Likutay Moharan Vol. 1) is a two-sentence teaching containing no bechina (parallel-aspect) declarations. The teaching opens with 'הַבְּגָדִים הֵם בְּסוֹד הַחַשְׁמַ"ל, שֶׁהוּא שְׁמִירָה' — Garments are in the secret/mystery (be-sod) of the Chashmal, which is protection. The term 'בְּסוֹד' denotes a kabbalistic mystical correspondence, not the structural bechina-equivalence that generates package-forming edges. The remainder of the text is purely eitza (cause-and-effect): because garments are the Chashmal-protection, torn garments corrupt that protection; because the garments embody the protective dimension, they hold the person accountable if dishonored. The second sentence is entirely practical-consequential. Torah #127 explicitly cross-references Torah #29 ('עַיֵּן לְעֵיל בְּסִימָן כט') for the full theological elaboration — Torah #29 contains the rich bechina-web (garments = malkhut, garments = speech-rectification, white garments = purity of Shekhinah, etc.). Torah #127 is a standalone practical reminder appended after that teaching, not a new conceptual structure. The absence of bechina-type relationships in Torah #127 is a genuine structural feature of this teaching, not a dataset gap.
